List the functions defined in packages

Source: R/pkg_functions.R
pkg_functions.Rd

Return one row per named function defined in the R source files of one or more packages, with its size, number of arguments and whether it is exported. Use it to find the largest functions, or to see how much of a package is internal.

Usage

pkg_functions(
  path = ".",
  include_ignored = FALSE,
  quiet = FALSE,
  cache = c("session", "persistent", "none")
)

Arguments

path

A character vector of packages. Each element is one of:

  • A local folder, such as "." or "~/code/mypkg". Use "local::path" to be explicit.

  • A GitHub repository, such as "r-lib/cli" or a github.com URL. Add @ref for a branch, tag or commit ("r-lib/cli@v3.6.0"). For a package in a subfolder, use the github:: prefix: "github::owner/repo/subdir".

  • A CRAN package, such as "desc". Add @version for an older release ("cran::desc@1.4.0"). Archived packages are supported.

Without a prefix, existing local folders take precedence, then "owner/repo" is treated as GitHub and a bare name as CRAN. A path that does not exist (e.g. "./mypkg") is an error, not a GitHub request.

With several packages, one that cannot be analysed (a typo, a failed download) does not stop the others: it is reported in a warning and returned as a row of NAs whose package is the specification as given (pkg_functions() leaves it out instead). A single package that fails, or all packages failing, is an error.

include_ignored

If TRUE, also analyse files matched by the package's .Rbuildignore. Version-control folders and R's built-in build exclusions are always skipped.

quiet

If TRUE, suppress progress messages.

cache

Where to keep downloaded GitHub and CRAN packages:

  • "session" (default): a temporary folder, removed when R closes.

  • "persistent": a user cache folder kept across R sessions. Only fixed versions are stored there: CRAN releases and GitHub refs that look like a commit SHA or a version tag ("owner/repo@v1.2.0"). Requests that can change over time (no ref, or a branch) always fetch the latest code and use the session cache instead.

  • "none": always download afresh.

Use pkg_cache_clear() to empty a cache.

Value

A tibble of class pkginspectr_functions with one row per function and columns:

  • package, version

  • file: path relative to the package root, e.g. "R/utils.R".

  • location: "R", "tests" or "other" (e.g. data-raw/).

  • name: the function's name.

  • line: the line where the definition starts.

  • code_lines: code lines in the definition, excluding comments and blank lines (as in pkg_lines()).

  • n_args: number of arguments, counting ... as one.

  • exported: whether the package's NAMESPACE exports the function, via export() or exportPattern(). NA for functions outside R/ or when the package has no readable NAMESPACE. S3 methods registered with S3method() are not exported in this sense.

Rows are ordered by package, file and line. A package without functions contributes no rows.

Details

A function is listed when it is assigned to a name at the top level of a file, with <-, = or <<-, written as function(...) or \(...). Functions defined inside other functions, inside lists or R6 classes, or with setMethod() are not listed. Files that fail to parse are skipped with a warning.

The same files are analysed as in pkg_lines(): R source files in R/, tests/ and data-raw/ that R CMD build would ship.

See also

pkg_lines() for package-level line counts.

Examples

fns <- pkg_functions(pkginspectr_example())
#> Listing functions in examplepkg...
fns
#> # pkginspectr: Functions, 3 functions in 1 package
#> # A tibble:    3 × 9
#>   package    version file     location name     line code_lines n_args exported
#>   <chr>      <chr>   <chr>    <chr>    <chr>   <int>      <int>  <int> <lgl>   
#> 1 examplepkg 1.2.3   R/funs.R R        add_one     5          3      1 TRUE    
#> 2 examplepkg 1.2.3   R/funs.R R        square     10          1      1 FALSE   
#> 3 examplepkg 1.2.3   R/funs.R R        compose    12          3      2 FALSE   

# The largest functions
fns[order(fns$code_lines, decreasing = TRUE), c("name", "code_lines")]
#> Warning: Unknown or uninitialised column: `package`.
#> # pkginspectr: Functions, 3 functions in 0 packages
#> # A tibble:    3 × 2
#>   name    code_lines
#>   <chr>        <int>
#> 1 add_one          3
#> 2 compose          3
#> 3 square           1

# Exported vs internal functions
table(fns$exported)
#> 
#> FALSE  TRUE 
#>     2     1 

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
# The ten longest functions in cli
pkg_functions("r-lib/cli", quiet = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::slice_max(code_lines, n = 10)
}
